media.prompt: Slow held workshop shot. Amber light on a worn oak bench. Hands pull a stitching awl through veg-tanned hide in steady rhythm. Close on a brass buckle catching the light. Wide bench view: waxed thread, bone folder, half-finished wallet. Steam from a beeswax pot. Sun drifts slowly across the surface. No fast cuts. Palette: warm tobacco, raw hide, deep shadow.
media.alt: Hands saddle-stitching a leather belt on a workshop bench in warm afternoon light

story: full-grain hide straight from the tannery
brass hardware and waxed linen thread
built to last thirty years not one season

founder.quote: I cut every piece myself and stitch it by hand — no machines, no shortcuts. The hide I use takes six weeks to tan in an oak bark pit, and you'll feel that density the first time you hold one of these belts.
founder.attribution: Jordan Merck, maker and sole proprietor

photo.prompt: Warm portrait of a leather worker at their bench, hands on a half-finished tote. Leather apron, rolled sleeves. Dark background with hand tools on a pegboard and a single amber work light. Quiet, focused, not posed. Warm grain.
